name: Salmon Wellington with Parmesan Spinach and Golden Puff Pastry Crust

instructions.primary_message: Remove pastry sheets from box and outer wrapping, then set on the counter to thaw slightly, 20-40 minutes. (The pastry is ready when it unfolds easily but is still cool to the touch.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
instructions.secondary_message:
1 lemon
1 (16 oz) pkg baby spinach
½ small bunch fresh dill

instructions.primary_message: Melt butter in a small saucepan set over medium-high heat; remove from heat. Zest lemon into the pan, then add Dijon, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine and set aside. (Reserve lemon for another use.)
instructions.secondary_message:
¼ cup butter, unsalted
1 ½ tbsp Dijon mustard
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add additional butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for it to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Cook until fully wilted, then remove from heat. Let cool, 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place egg and water in a small bowl, then beat with a whisk or fork to combine the egg wash. Set aside.
Finely grate Parmesan. Place in a medium bowl.
Shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the Parmesan, along with spices, and stir to combine.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ tsp garlic powder
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Using your hands, squeeze as much water from the cooled spinach as you can, then roughly chop. Add to the bowl with Parmesan and dill, then stir to combine. Set aside.

If using salmon with skin, place the fillet, skin-side down, on a cutting board. Holding the tail end (or corner) firmly, use a knife to cut between the flesh and skin; continue to cut through the length of the fillet (take care not to cut through the skin); discard the skin. Pat salmon dry with paper towels, then season both sides with salt and pepper. Set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
24 oz salmon fillet
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Line a large baking sheet pan with parchment paper.

Lightly dust a work surface with flour. Working one by one, roll out each pastry sheet into a 9 x 13-inch rectangle. Transfer one sheet to the baking sheet and brush with half of the lemon-Dijon butter, leaving a 2-inch border all the way around. (Reserve remaining butter for later use.)
Spoon the Parmesan spinach on top of the buttered pastry, spreading it out in an even layer (make sure to leave the 2-inch border all the way around the pastry).
Arrange salmon on top of the spinach, then brush the fish with the remaining butter. Brush the exposed edges of the pastry with half of the egg wash. (Reserve remaining egg wash for later use.)

Cover salmon with the remaining pastry sheet, sealing it to the bottom pastry sheet with your fingers. Trim any uneven edges of the pastry with a knife, then seal the edges using the tines of a fork (or your fingers). If desired, score a crosshatch pattern into the top of the pastry using the tip of a knife (making sure not to cut all the way through the pastry).
Brush pastry all over with the reserved egg wash. Place salmon wellington in the refrigerator to firm up for 30 minutes.
When the salmon wellington is done chilling, preheat oven to 425°F.

Place salmon wellington in the preheated oven and bake until pastry is golden and slightly risen, about 20 minutes. Reduce oven to 400°F and continue to bake until pastry is golden brown and cooked through, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Let salmon wellington stand for 10 minutes before slicing and serving. Enjoy!
